matches.rationale: GT1 concerns contradictory claims about SNN position error (0.04m claimed superior vs. oscillatory/reduced reliability) in Table 3 and Section 5.3. None of the findings address this specific inconsistency about position control performance claims.

GT2 identifies that the BC term is inside the warm-up indicator in Equation 1, preventing BC loss during warm-up and contradicting the stated purpose. No finding addresses this specific equation structure or the BC term placement issue.

GT3 concerns missing seed/evaluation protocol details in Table 4 ablation study compared to Figure 4's stated protocol. No finding addresses this asymmetry in experimental reporting between main results and ablation study.
GT4 concerns the unsupported '2.1× improvement' claim in the abstract regarding slope effects. No finding addresses this specific quantitative claim or its lack of support in Figure 3.
GT5 identifies misattribution of the fast sigmoid approximation to reference [27] (SuperSpike paper). No finding addresses this specific misattribution of the fast sigmoid surrogate gradient method.
GT6 concerns missing safety protocols and ethical considerations for real-world drone experiments with expected crashes. No finding addresses safety measures or ethical integrity issues.
GT7 concerns overly promotional language in the abstract ('set to revolutionize', 'orders-of-magnitude'). No finding addresses rhetorical presentation or promotional language issues.

Both GT8 and pred_id 1 identify the same cross-section inconsistency about action history usage: Section 3.1 states the critic receives action history, while Section 3.4 states it does not. This is the identical scientific issue about privileged information in the critic architecture.

GT9 concerns exaggeration of baseline performance in text (claiming baselines fail to exceed -200 points when Figure 4a shows -100 to -150). No finding addresses this specific misrepresentation of baseline rewards.

Both GT10 and pred_id 5 identify the same issue with Equation 7's adaptive slope scheduler: the derivative r′_{t−i} is undefined/unspecified, making the equation non-reproducible. Both note the lack of specification for how this derivative is computed.
GT11 concerns the 3.3× training duration disparity in Table 6 (1000 vs 300 epochs) creating unfair comparison. No finding addresses this specific asymmetry in computational budget between methods.

GT12 concerns misinterpretation of gradient randomness as beneficial exploration noise in Section 5.1, conflating random gradients with parameter noise. No finding addresses this specific claim interpretation issue.

GT13 identifies unsupported 'significant energy savings' claim attributed to reference [18] which doesn't provide quantitative energy measurements. Pred_id 7 addresses a different energy claim ([23]/PopSAN), not this DSQN/Loihi reference.

Both GT14 and pred_id 4 identify the unfair architectural comparison in Table 2: GT14 notes ANN [64-64] vs SNN [256-128] with 4× parameter difference, while pred_id 4 identifies the caption claims 256-128 for both but ANN data is inconsistent. Both address the same table's architectural comparison issue.

GT15 concerns the abstract omitting the guiding policy dependency limitation that is acknowledged in the conclusion. No finding addresses this cross-section inconsistency between abstract framing and conclusion limitations.
GT16 concerns overstated claim of 'advancing theoretical understanding' in the conclusion when contributions are primarily empirical. No finding addresses this rhetorical overstatement issue.

GT17 concerns the soft-reset mechanism in Equation 4 potentially producing negative membrane potentials, creating physical implausibility. No finding addresses this specific equation or the soft-reset mechanism issue.
GT18 concerns missing curriculum learning details in Table 5 (total epochs, transition triggers, interpolation schedule). No finding addresses these missing curriculum protocol specifications.
GT19 concerns unsupported sim-to-real transfer claim in Section 5.3 without evidence of domain randomization or adaptation techniques. No finding addresses this specific transfer learning claim.

GT20 concerns suspiciously low variance in Table 4 for failed configurations (32±1.2, 36±4.1) being statistically implausible. No finding addresses this specific variance pattern issue in the ablation study.
